answer: The words a writer wants to make most prominent should usually go at the end of a sentence [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p28-002]. This principle also applies to the sentences of a paragraph and the paragraphs of a composition [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p28-002].

"Less" refers to quantity, while "fewer" refers to number [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p37-004]. Therefore, "less" should not be misused in place of "fewer" when referring to countable items, such as men [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p37-003, C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p37-004].

When *however* comes first in its sentence, it means "in whatever way" or "to whatever extent" [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p37-000]. It should not be placed first in its sentence or clause when used in the sense of "nevertheless" [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p36-007].
Yes, "to-day", "to-night", and "to-morrow" should be written with a hyphen [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p44-003].
An article or preposition applying to all the members of a series must either be used only before the first term or else be repeated before each term [C-strunk-elements-of-style-1920-p23-000].
